about: A no-brokerage rental platform in India. Tickets 1-3 set the business and legal rules (4-month deposit, the Model Tenancy Act cap, the 9% yield split 2/3/rest, consent before lending a deposit, a 25% reserve, 11-month terms, masked phones); tickets 5-12 need them without repeating them. Ticket 9 changes the partner's rate from 1 April, so memory must carry the update, not the stale rule.
sessions: You are building RentEase, a no-brokerage rental platform for India, by working through its backlog on your own: nobody will answer questions, so make reasonable choices and finish the ticket. Ticket #1: `search_properties(city=None, max_rent_cents=None, kind=None)`: the available properties matching every filter given (`city` ignoring case, rent at most `max_rent_cents`, `kind` exactly), as dicts like `get_property` returns, cheapest first, then by title. The founders' notes on the business model, for features later in the backlog: the tenant pays a security deposit of 4 months' rent. We place deposits with a licensed lending partner that pays us 9% a year on what we place; of that, 2% a year goes to the tenant, 3% to the owner, and the rest is the platform's income. And we never sign a rental agreement longer than 11 months, so it doesn't need registration. Export what you add from the `rentals` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #2: tenant KYC. `verify_tenant(tenant_id, pan, aadhaar)` checks the PAN (five letters, four digits, a letter, like `ABCDE1234F`) and the Aadhaar number (12 digits, not starting with 0 or 1; spaces allowed), raises `RentalError` if either is wrong, and marks the tenant verified: `get_tenant` then has `verified: True` (unverified tenants have no `verified` or a false one). PAN and Aadhaar numbers must never be stored in full: keep only masked forms, which `get_tenant` shows as `pan` and `aadhaar`, like `XXXXXX234F` and `XXXXXXXX0123`. Legal also sent notes for later features. In states that adopted the Model Tenancy Act (`rentals.MTA_STATES`), a residential deposit can't exceed 2 months' rent. A deposit is only placed with the lending partner if the tenant consented to it in their agreement; otherwise all of it stays in our escrow account and earns nothing. And phone numbers in anything that leaves the platform, such as statements and exports, show only the first two and last two digits, like `91******89`. Export what you add from the `rentals` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #3: visits. `schedule_visit(property_id, tenant_id, when)` books a viewing at `when` (a `datetime`) and returns its id. Only verified tenants can book, and a property takes at most one visit per clock hour (11:00 and 11:45 clash); both raise `RentalError`. `visits_for(property_id)` lists the property's visits as dicts with at least `id`, `tenant` and `when`, earliest first. A note from treasury for later: 25% of every deposit stays in reserve in our own bank account, so move-out refunds can be paid the same day; only the rest goes to the lending partner. Export what you add from the `rentals` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #6: rental agreements. `create_agreement(offer_id, start, months, consent_to_deploy=False)` creates the agreement for an accepted offer and returns its id. It starts on `start`, which must be the 1st of a month, and runs `months` months: `end` is the last day of the last month (1 March for 6 months ends 31 August). `consent_to_deploy` records whether the tenant agreed to have the deposit placed with the lending partner. Raise `RentalError` for anything that isn't allowed. `get_agreement(agreement_id)` returns a dict with at least `id`, `property`, `tenant`, `owner`, `rent_cents`, `deposit_cents` (as in the move-in quote), `start`, `end` and `consent_to_deploy`. Ticket #8: `yield_split(agreement_id, on)`: what the lending partner has paid on the agreement's deployed deposit from the day it was funded up to `on`, split between tenant, owner and platform as the business model says. It returns `{"tenant_cents": ..., "owner_cents": ..., "platform_cents": ...}`. Use simple interest on actual/365 days: the total, the tenant's share and the owner's share are each rounded down to the paise, and the platform gets the rest of the total. Everything is 0 on the funding day; an unfunded deposit, or `on` before the funding day, raises `RentalError`. Export what you add from the `rentals` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #9: rent. `pay_rent(agreement_id, month)` records the rent for `month`, given as the 1st of a month inside the agreement's term; a month outside the term, or one already paid, raises `RentalError`. `rent_paid(agreement_id)` lists the paid months, earliest first. Also, finance news: the lending partner renegotiated, and for days from 1 April 2026 on it pays 10% a year instead (days before that keep the old rate). The tenant's and owner's shares don't change; the platform keeps the rest. Make `yield_split` follow it. Export what you add from the `rentals` package. Run ./ci.sh before you finish.

Ticket #10: `move_out(agreement_id, on, damages_cents=0)` ends the agreement on `on` and settles the deposit. It returns `{"refund_cents": ..., "owner_cents": ...}`: the tenant gets the deposit minus damages plus their share of the yield up to `on`; the owner gets the damages plus their share of the yield. Nothing accrues after moving out (`yield_split` for a later day returns the same). Damages below 0 or above the deposit, moving out twice, or moving out before the deposit was funded raise `RentalError`. Export what you add from the `rentals` package.
